# New renderings and departures, iliad-049 (8.292–380)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσεφώνεε Τεῦκρος ἀμύμων (8.292, whole-line reply-formula) | "To him answering spoke Teucer, blameless:" | "In answer blameless Teucer spoke to him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); follows the Odyssey table's τὸν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσεφώνεε … row; ἀμύμων "blameless" as in the table |
| τὴν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε θεὰ γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (8.357, whole-line reply-formula) | "Her then in turn addressed the goddess, gleaming-eyed Athena:" | "Then the goddess, gleaming-eyed Athena, spoke to her in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); follows the table's τὴν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε … (6.440, 7.37) |
| τοὺς δὲ ἰδοῦσ’ ἐλέησε θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη (8.350) | "And them seeing, pitied the goddess, white-armed Hera," | "And the goddess, white-armed Hera, pitied them when she saw them," | "took pity on", "felt sorry"; ἐλεέω "pity" as in the table's ἐλεαίρει "pities"; λευκώλενος "white-armed" as in the table |
| αἶψα δ’ Ἀθηναίην ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (8.351) | "and at once to Athena winged words she spoke:" | "and at once she spoke winged words to Athena:" | follows the table's αὐτίκ’ Ἀθηναίην ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (4.69); αἶψα is "at once" as αὐτίκα |
| ἀρηϊθόων αἰζηῶν (8.298) | "war-swift vigorous young men" | "strong young men, swift in war" | "Ares-swift" (makes Ares a god in the compound), "warlike", "battle-eager"; ἀρηΐθοος is probably Ἄρης "war" + θοός "swift", the first part is not certain and the note says so; αἰζηός "vigorous young man" / "strong young men" as in the table (5.92) |
| κύνα λυσσητῆρα (8.299) | "frenzied dog" | "frenzied dog" | "mad dog" (suggests rabies), "raging dog", "raving cur"; "rage" is kept clear of the wrath-words; λυσσητήρ is from λύσσα "wild frenzy", and κύων is "dog" as in the table |
| ἐῢν Πριάμοιο υἱόν (8.303) | "the good son of Priam" | "the good son of Priam" | "noble", "fine"; follows the table's ἐῢς πάϊς Ἀγχίσαο "the good son" |
| μήκων … καρπῷ βριθομένη νοτίῃσί τε εἰαρινῇσιν (8.306–307) | "weighed down with fruit and with the moist of spring" | "weighed down with its fruit and the damp of spring" | "spring rains" (names rain, which νοτίη "moisture" does not), "seed-pod" (καρπός stays "fruit") |
| τόν … εἴασε (8.317, line also found elsewhere with κεῖσθαι; departure from "allowed") | "him indeed then he let be, though grieving for his companion," | "Then he let him be, though he grieved for his companion," | "allowed" (the published English of the same line elsewhere, where εἴασε has κεῖσθαι "to lie"; here there is no infinitive, so "allowed" has no object). The remaining words of the line (ἀχνύμενός περ ἑταίρου "though grieving for his companion") are kept as published. |
| ὃ δ’ ἄρ’ οὐκ ἀπίθησεν ἀκούσας (8.319) | "and he then did not disobey, having heard." | "and he did not disobey when he heard." | "was not unwilling", "did not refuse"; οὐκ ἀπίθησε "did not disobey" as in 2.166 |
| πικρὸν ὀϊστόν (8.323) | "a bitter arrow" | "a bitter arrow" | the table's row (4.118), the article dropped to match the Greek |
| κληῒς (8.325) | "collarbone" | "collarbone" | "key", "clavicle", "shoulder-bone" |
| μάλιστα δὲ καίριόν ἐστι (8.326) | "and it is the deadliest place" | "where a blow is most deadly" | "the most vital spot", "most fatal" (καίριον is "at the right place; deadly"; the word is kept as "deadly", the place noun is supplied only in `l`) |
| λίθῳ ὀκριόεντι (8.327) | "a jagged stone" | "a jagged stone" | "rough", "sharp-edged", "angular"; ὀκριόεις is "rough, jagged" (ὄκρις "point") |
| κασιγνήτοιο πεσόντος (8.330) | "his brother, who had fallen" | "his brother, who had fallen" | "his fallen kinsman"; κασίγνητος is "brother" as in the Odyssey table |
| ἀπερωεύς (ἐμῶν μενέων ἀπερωεύς, 8.361) | "a thwarter of my might" | "a thwarter of my might" | "a hinderer", "one who keeps off", "an obstructer"; the word is rare and its sense is not fully known, the note says so; μένος keeps "might" (the plural μενέων is "might" too) |
| σχέτλιος, αἰὲν ἀλιτρός (8.361) | "cruel, always sinful" | "cruel, always sinful" | "wretched", "always a wrongdoer", "offender"; σχέτλιος "cruel" as in the table; ἀλιτρός is "one who offends (against gods or men)", kept as "sinful" |
| πευκαλίμῃσι φρεσίν (8.366) | "keen wits" | "my keen wits" | "sharp" (reserved for ἐχεπευκής), "shrewd" (reserved for πυκινός), "wise"; the sense of πευκαλίμος is not fully known, and "keen" is only the traditional gloss; φρένες "wits" |
| ἐξ Ἐρέβευς … κύνα στυγεροῦ Ἀΐδαο (8.368) | "out of Erebus the dog of hateful Hades" | "out of Erebus the dog of hateful Hades" | "Cerberus" (the poet withholds the name); Ἀΐδης "Hades" as in the table |
| Στυγὸς ὕδατος αἰπὰ ῥέεθρα (8.369) | "the steep streams of the water of the Styx" | "the steep streams of the water of the Styx" | "sheer", "high" (αἰπύς is "steep, sheer"); follows the table's Στυγὸς ὕδατος "the water of the Styx" |
| πτολίπορθον (Ἀχιλλῆα πτολίπορθον, 8.372) | "Achilles the city-sacking" | "Achilles, the city-sacker" | "city-sacking Achilles", "sacker of cities" (the table's 16.442 noun-phrase pattern is followed here because the epithet stands after the name) |
| φίλην γλαυκώπιδα (8.373) | "his dear gleaming-eyed one" | "his dear gleaming-eyed one" | "his dear owl-eyed girl", "his dear Athena", "grey-eyed"; γλαυκῶπις as a noun is "gleaming-eyed one", as for the epithet in the table |
| ἐπέντυε μώνυχας ἵππους (8.374) | "make ready the solid-hoofed horses" | "make ready the solid-hoofed horses" | "harness", "yoke", "prepare"; μώνυχας ἵππους "solid-hoofed horses" as in the table (5.236) |
| πολέμοιο γεφύρας (8.378) | "the bridges of war" | "the bridges of war" | "the ridges of battle", "the causeways of war", "the lines"; the meaning of γεφύρας here is not known, and the note says so |
| κορέει κύνας ἠδ’ οἰωνούς δημῷ καὶ σάρκεσσι (8.379–380) | "will sate dogs and birds with fat and with flesh" | "will glut dogs and birds with his fat and flesh" | "feed", "fill"; κορέννυμι "sate"; δημός "fat" as in the table (8.240) |

No other new recurring formula; the remaining stock phrases (ἐρίηρες ἑταῖροι, δῖος, καλλίτριχες ἵπποι, κάρη κομόωντες Ἀχαιοί, βροτολοιγὸς Ἄρης, αἰγίοχος Ζεύς, κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ, γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη, λευκώλενος Ἥρη, ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα, ἦ ῥα καί, σμερδαλέα ἰάχων, μώνυχες ἵπποι, γλαφυραὶ νῆες) follow the house table unchanged. Lines 8.314 and 8.316 are published units word for word (identical `l` and `i`); line 8.354 sits inside a longer unit with the published wording kept ("who indeed, having filled up an evil fate, shall perish" / "who will fill up an evil fate and perish"). No Odyssey line in this part has a different English here.
